entities.title: The timeout kills only the command itself
entities.summary: After --timeout, SIGKILL goes to the command's own process, not to the processes it started; once the command exits, the output pipe is waited on for at most 2 seconds.
entities.impact: Children of a timed-out command (or background children of a finished one) may keep running, and output they write after those 2 seconds is not shown.

entities.title: Standard output and error are merged
entities.summary: The command's standard output and error share one pipe, so the result cannot say which stream a line came from, and nothing is shown until the command ends.
entities.impact: A caller that needs the streams apart, or live output, should run the command directly.

entities.title: At most 64 MiB of output
entities.summary: Output past 64 MiB is read and discarded; the footer says it was not read.
entities.impact: The end of a very long output is lost.
